applies_why: The judge does not rest STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED on a single verse failing to state a link or its contrary; it rests on the defender having dropped the curse limb, leaving no live link to contradict.
quote: D6 vs C4 (Jeremiah 22:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- C4 pressed against the curse limb the defender dropped in [CR3] LINK 5, so no live link remains to contradict; the dropping is recorded there.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED" — I weighed whether "no live link remains to contradict" is such a single-verse non-statement ground or instead a dropped-limb/live-link ground.
why: The judge's stated ground is the dropped curse limb and absence of a live link to contradict, not that a single verse fails to state a link or its contrary.
